g_policy.reason: The card is opt-in (the user taps to play) and the offer copy states the reward (3 Advanced reasoning answers today). 'Not now' leaves home unchanged, and the ad-fail path is defined.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 3 Advanced reasoning mode answers, which have no cash value and cannot be withdrawn or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is the first app open after 3 or more days without a session, by a non-subscriber. That is an app event and needs no chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal says it removes nothing free, and it adds a sample of a paywalled feature without capping anything free today.

g_brand_safety.reason: The card is app chrome on s01 (rated safe), placed above the prompt card and outside any message list or thread, so it is not in a conversation.

c1_revealed_value.reason: Advanced reasoning mode is listed as a Luzia+ paywall bullet (s02.e03, l02), so the app charges for the resource the reward grants.

c2_evidence.reason: The cited claims are observed: s02.e03 lists Advanced reasoning mode on the paywall, s01.e02 is the home upsell badge, and s02.e19 is the trial button. The reward is labeled as an inference, not presented as an observed mechanic.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward is limited to 3 answers and expires at midnight, so it is a quantity- and time-limited sample rather than unlimited access.

c5_moment.reason: The card appears on the home screen at app open, before the user starts a task, and is dismissible, so it does not interrupt anything.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn sponsored game. The reward is granted after a confirmed play (an unconfirmed play shows 'didn't count'), and the trigger is a detectable session-gap app event.

c7_specific.reason: It names Luzia's Advanced reasoning mode (s02.e03), the home Luzia+ badge, the 'How can I help you today?' prompt card and the 3-day trial button, so it is specific to this app.

other_concern: How Advanced reasoning mode works for a free user (whether there is a toggle, and how a metered sample would be enforced) was not observed. The proposal's claim that answers cost real model time is also an inference.
